newsitem.title: JAPAN: FCC's Hundt says Japan's connection rates too high.
newsitem.headline: FCC's Hundt says Japan's connection rates too high.

text.p: The top phone regulator in the United States on Tuesday criticised Japan for its "record level" telephone interconnection charges.

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt told reporters in Tokyo that Japan should introduce a more aggressive interconnection policy, speed up its licensing process and invite more foreign competitors into the domestic market.

He said Japan's interconnection charges, such as those charged to connect local call networks and international calls to local call networks, are "all at record levels relative to (other) developed countries".
"I haven't heard any opinion from anyone to explain why those record levels would be justified," Hundt said.
He also said more competition was going to be needed if the planned splitting up of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp proceeded as set out under the current proposals.

"If you are going to go with the British approach (by not truly splitting it up), you have to try to get competition in other ways...to allow competitive infrastructures to just come into the country and get them going."

Hundt said the interconnection charge for wireless phone operators to connect to the Baby Bell networks in the United States was about 0.3 cent per minute, compared to eight yen (about seven cents) in Japan.
The so-called international settlement rates, charged to complete international call rates, are about 10 cents in Britain, compared to 40 cents in Japan, Hundt said.

Hundt, in Japan after visiting India and Israel to discuss the international settlement issue, said he has requested Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry and agencies in other countries to put together an agenda for the next round of global telecommunications talks.
The topics would include ways to achieve virtually the same interconnection charges around the world.
